C1a: high: CME or a regulator describes the product as predominantly retail, or a sourced retail/uninformed share of volume >= 40%; proxy accepted: CFTC COT nonreportable share of open interest >= 0.40 in the standard window (or the only window the sheet has), flagged as an OI proxy.

low: COT nonreportable share of OI < 0.15 (reportable large traders, i.e. commercials, swap dealers, managed money, dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, then hold more than 85% of OI), or a source documenting professional dominance of the volume.

medium: nonreportable 0.15 to 0.40, and every unknown (spec default). A CME line that markets a product to retail or individual traders without saying it is predominantly retail does not reach high; CFTC 'small trader' volume shares (accounts under 0.5% of daily volume) are not retail shares.
C1b: high: any one documented for THIS product (separate book): an exchange market-maker, liquidity-provider or fee-incentive programme for liquidity provision in force in or around the 2023-11..2024-02 pilot window or now (a volume rebate for retail brokers is not a liquidity-provision incentive); documented HFT or electronic-market-maker dominance, read as an automated (ATS) share of about 60% or more of the product's volume (product row, or a group row that contains the product, flagged), or PTF/EMM shares of that size; a sourced spread at or averaging within about 1.2 ticks of one tick most of the time with a sourced best-level depth of tens of contracts or more.
low: none of the high items, no programme found, and at least one of 'few HFT documented' or 'spread usually wider than 1 tick' sourced.
medium: none of the high items and the only known fact is a negative programme search (or programmes that ended years before 2023) with HFT share and spread unknown.
high (spec unknown default): nothing at all sourced. Sibling or cousin books are not used for (b); options market-maker programmes do not count for the futures book.
C6: Qualifying evidence: a study showing short-horizon (seconds to minutes, the strategy's and the pilot's markout scale) prediction of a PRICE move (mid, trade price, return, price flip) from order-book variables (OFI, queue imbalance, trade signs, LOB features), or passive liquidity provision profitable NET of costs.

Not qualifying: descriptive work, price-discovery or information shares, contemporaneous impact, spread/volatility/liquidity prediction, gross-only realized spreads, bar-based signals, horizons of hours, days or weeks.
4: qualifying positive on SAME or SIBLING; 3: on COUSIN; 2: on CLASS; 1: none qualifying found.

0: a study on THIS product (SAME; the spec's anchor 0 says 'on this product' without the sibling extension of anchor 4) whose result is that order-book predictability is absent or arbitraged away, or passive provision unprofitable net of costs, with no qualifying positive on SAME or SIBLING. Studies documenting only that naive passive fills are adversely selected (adverse selection is part of the gross edge the pilot measures) are not anchor-0 evidence.
Abstract-only items are counted and flagged. A study positive 'for some contracts' without saying which is credited at the COUSIN level (3) even when coded SIBLING.
Each rating with a plausible alternative reading carries the alternative score in flags.
